gloss: Japanese era calendar; Japanese imperial calendar

definitions.gloss: Japanese era calendar; Japanese imperial calendar
definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese way of counting years based on imperial reign names ({元号|げんごう}), e.g., {令和|れいわ} 8 for 2026. Used alongside the Western calendar ({西暦|せいれき}) in official documents and daily life.

examples.japanese: {和暦|われき}で{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write it in the Japanese era calendar.

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}は{和暦|われき}と{西暦|せいれき}の{両方|りょうほう}で{記入|きにゅう}する。
examples.english: Fill in the document using both the Japanese era calendar and the Western calendar.

examples.japanese: {役所|やくしょ}では{今|いま}も{和暦|われき}が{広|ひろ}く{使用|しよう}されている。
examples.english: At government offices, the Japanese era calendar is still widely used.

notes:
Years are counted from the start of each emperor's reign and prefixed with the era name ({元号|げんごう}): e.g., {令和|れいわ}{元年|がんねん} (Reiwa 1 = 2019), {平成|へいせい}30{年|ねん} (Heisei 30 = 2018).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和暦|われき}で{書|か}く: to write in the Japanese calendar
- {和暦|われき}に{変換|へんかん}する: to convert to the Japanese calendar
- {和暦|われき}と{西暦|せいれき}: Japanese and Western calendars

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {西暦|せいれき}: Western (Gregorian) calendar — the counterpart, used worldwide
- {元号|げんごう}: era name itself (e.g., {令和|れいわ}, {平成|へいせい})
